outcomes.text: Explore published play extracts closely, relating interpretations to the complete play and justifying performance ideas.
Understand original-period or modern-revival performance characteristics and apply them when interpreting a play.
Develop ideas for performing a role, working in an ensemble, directing scenes and designing appropriate elements.
Approach a complete play practically by considering how actors, designers and directors could interpret and stage it.
Anticipate the intended audience effects of artistic choices in performance.
Understand a play’s theatrical genre, tradition, historical context and performance history.
Use theatre-practice knowledge to develop original performing, designing and directing ideas from the text.
Explain a text’s performance potential clearly, supporting ideas with relevant textual detail.
Develop vocal and physical acting skills for a scripted extract.
Create characterisation appropriate to the scripted piece’s genre and style.
Control the pace of a scripted performance and work effectively as an ensemble.
Develop audience awareness and communicate effectively with live spectators.
Create and perform a solo programme for a live audience using at least three thematically connected extracts from existing texts.
Select suitable material around a theme and connect it into an integrated performance with effective links.
Apply acting skills appropriate to the selected material and guide the audience through the chosen sequence of texts.
Use lighting, sound, puppetry, masks, props or costume appropriately within an individual performance.
Create linking material to be spoken as part of the individual performance.
Interpret the selected stimulus creatively and exploit its potential for dramatic development.
Interact effectively with other performers and support them appropriately during ensemble work.
Contribute to a dramatically effective structure using features such as openings, endings, transitions, reversals or circularity.
Create and communicate a clear, sustained role that remains consistent with the piece’s style and connects with the audience.
Analyse the devising process and identify the artistic intentions of the piece.
Evaluate how your personal contribution helped the devised piece achieve its artistic intentions.
Understand and interpret the role being performed.
Use vocal, physical and movement skills appropriately for the role.
Engage and communicate effectively with the audience during performance.
Engage with other performers while performing.
Use a poem or pair of short poems as the starting point for devised drama.
Use a short story as the starting point for devised drama.
Use a speech or brief episode from a published play as a stimulus for devising.
Use a novel’s opening paragraph as a stimulus for devised drama.
Research and explore a chosen stimulus for dramatic possibilities, structure and effectiveness.
Use a painting, photograph or sculpture as a stimulus for devised drama.
Use a short piece of music as a stimulus for devised drama.
Create and communicate a role while devising a performance from a selected stimulus.
Build a strong ensemble within a devised performance.
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of devised work and reflect on its process and artistic intentions.
Understand the social, historical, cultural and theatrical context in which a chosen practitioner, tradition or style developed.
Understand the cultural purpose, political intentions and artistic ideals of drama associated with the chosen practitioner, tradition or style.
Understand the practitioner’s methods, preferred venues, audience configuration and approaches to theatrical work.
Understand how directors, actors and designers contribute to productions associated with the chosen practitioner, tradition or style.
Review relevant productions and projects, studying one in depth through production history, photographs or archival recordings.
Use a practitioner, tradition or style as a starting point to devise original drama that clearly reflects its influence.
Develop a case study statement explaining the basis and intentions of the devised work.
Take responsibility, individually and collaboratively, for developing a complete devised performance.
Develop practical experience using simple props, costume, set, lighting or sound when appropriate.
Analyse and evaluate work created for a group devised performance.
Choose one prescribed practitioner, theatre tradition or style as the basis for group devising.
Investigate a particular professional production representing the chosen practitioner, tradition or style.
Investigate one professionally performed current or historic production associated with the selected practitioner, tradition or style.
Devise and perform group drama for a live audience, working as either performers or designers.
Develop appropriate performance and design skills for the devised production.
Apply lighting, sound, costume, mask, set or prop design skills where appropriate.
Research a chosen area of theatre and drama, focusing on the practicalities of theatre-making and performance.
Investigate two performance texts, a theatre genre, a practitioner across multiple works, or a performance style across several pieces.
Explore performance, movement, music or dance, design, directing, production history or audience in relation to the chosen subject.
Write a structured research essay that may combine clear written expression with visual or diagrammatic material.
Analyse, evaluate and reflect on dramatic and theatrical possibilities throughout the research process.
Independently write a 2500–3000-word essay exploring, analysing and evaluating a focused area of theatre-making and performance.
Choose an original topic, excluding Component 1 set texts, and formulate a specific question with the teacher.
Focus the investigation on the practical processes of theatre-making and performance.
Investigate two complete performance texts, a theatre genre, a practitioner across multiple works, or a performance style across several works.
Study performing roles or chorus, movement or choreography, music or dance, design, directing, production history, or audience.
Frame the essay title as a question or statement followed by a prompt encouraging further exploration.
Ensure the title offers enough range and depth for detailed academic investigation.
Select and apply research methods suited to the chosen topic and subject area.
Use appropriate methods such as literature reviews, performance records, interviews, archives, practice-based research, or observation.
Critically reflect on research methods and evaluate the reliability and relevance of sources.
Engage with research findings reflectively and critically.
Present findings using academic writing conventions, thorough source referencing, and a complete bibliography.
Understand the meaning and importance of plagiarism.
Reference every source used in the research.
Reference quotations and sources in the text, then list all sources fully and consistently in a recognised bibliography style.
Exclude the bibliography from the essay word count.
